problem.title: One truck. Two trips. Only one of them paid.
problem.lead: A truck that carries goods from the Terai up to the hills often has nothing to carry back. The driver still buys diesel, pays tolls and spends a long day on the road, for an empty trip.

cards.title: Owners lose a day's earnings
cards.body: An empty return eats into the profit from the loaded trip, and waiting at a truck yard for a return load can take days.

cards.title: Shippers pay for both ways
cards.body: When a truck expects to come back empty, the price of the trip has to cover the return too.

cards.title: Empty kilometres cost everyone
cards.body: Every empty trip burns diesel and adds a truck to busy hill roads without moving anything.

problem.answer: FLITO shows truck owners the loads going their way, including the way home, and lets shippers find trucks that are already headed there. More trips carry goods both ways, so prices can be fairer for everyone.

how.title: Simple for every kind of user

stories.title: How a trip plays out
stories.lead: Three everyday journeys, start to finish.
stories.note: These are examples that show how FLITO is used. They are not stories of real customers.

items.title: The trip home that paid for itself
items.body: An owner from Butwal delivers rice to Kathmandu. Before heading back, they open FLITO, find a load of furniture going to Butwal and send an offer. The shipper accepts, and the return trip pays for its own diesel.

items.title: Cement for a new house
items.body: A family building a house in Pokhara needs 600 bags of cement from Hetauda, too much for one truck. They post the load for two trucks, get three offers by evening, accept the two best from verified owners, and watch both trucks climb towards Mugling on the map.

items.title: A whole job on one screen
items.body: A driver who has never used email logs in with a phone number and PIN. One job, one big button at each stop: arrived, loaded, delivered. A photo of the goods, the receiver signs on the phone, and the job is done.

trust.title: Trust is built into every booking
trust.lead: You are handing your goods, or your truck, to someone you may never have met. FLITO makes sure you know who they are.
points: Owners and drivers are checked against their ID before they can make offers or take jobs
Trucks are checked against their bluebook and papers
Phone numbers are shown only to the people on a booking
Every step of the trip, from arrival to delivery, is shown to everyone on the booking as it happens
Shippers and owners rate each other after every trip

cta.title: Ready when your next load is.
cta.lead: Create a free account in about two minutes. No email needed: a phone number and PIN are enough.

steps.title: Post your load
steps.body: Say what you are sending, how much it weighs, where it is going, when, and how many trucks it needs. Add photos if they help. It takes about two minutes.

steps.title: Get offers
steps.body: Verified truck owners heading that way offer a price for each truck. Accept the ones you want, or pick a matched truck and ask its owner at your own price.

steps.title: Book and track
steps.body: Each accepted offer is a booking for that truck. Call the driver in one tap and follow the truck on the map.

steps.title: Confirm delivery
steps.body: The driver photographs the goods and your receiver signs on the phone. Then rate the trip.

steps.title: Add your trucks
steps.body: Register each truck as it appears on its bluebook: type, capacity, where it is based and the areas it serves.

steps.title: Get verified
steps.body: Upload your ID, your PAN and each truck's papers. The FLITO team checks them before you can send offers.

steps.title: Find loads and send offers
steps.body: See loads that fit your trucks, including loads for the return trip, and offer a price for each truck you can send.

steps.title: Assign a driver
steps.body: When a shipper accepts, pick the driver for the job. It appears on their phone right away.

steps.title: Log in with your phone
steps.body: Your truck owner adds you with your phone number. Log in with it and a 4-digit PIN. No email needed.

steps.title: See your job
steps.body: Pickup, drop-off, the goods and the shipper's number, all on one screen.

steps.title: One button at each stop
steps.body: Tap when you arrive, when you have loaded and when you have delivered. The shipper sees each step.

steps.title: Prove the delivery
steps.body: Take a photo of the goods and get the receiver's signature on the phone. Job done.

hero.title: How FLITO works
hero.lead: From posting a load to the receiver's signature, here is what happens at every step, for every kind of user.

shipper: A phone number or an email address
What you are sending and roughly how much it weighs
owner: Your citizenship, national ID, passport or driving license
Each truck's bluebook details and photos
driver: A phone number your truck owner has added

lifecycle.title: What every status means
lifecycle.lead: Everyone on a booking sees the same status, and each change sends a notification.

items.title: Pending
items.body: An offer was accepted and the booking was made. The owner now assigns a driver and truck.

items.title: Confirmed
items.body: A driver and truck are assigned and the pickup is planned. Everyone can call each other.

items.title: In transit
items.body: The goods are loaded and on the road. The driver's location is shared while the trip lasts.

items.title: Completed
items.body: Delivered, with photos and the receiver's signature. Shipper and owner rate each other.

items.title: Cancelled
items.body: The shipper or the owner cancelled before the goods were loaded. The truck's place on the load opens again, and phone numbers are hidden.

offers.title: How prices are agreed
offers.lead: There are no fixed rates on FLITO, and no haggling back and forth: every offer is accepted or declined at its price.

points.title: An owner offers a price
points.body: Only verified owners can offer: one price for each truck they can send, and never more trucks than the load still needs.

points.title: Or the shipper names a price
points.body: A shipper can pick a matched truck and ask its owner to carry the load at the shipper's price. The owner accepts or declines.

points.title: Offers don't wait forever
points.body: An offer stays open for 48 hours, and never longer than its load. A load takes offers until the end of its pickup day.

points.title: Each acceptance books a truck
points.body: Every accepted offer is its own booking. When all the trucks a load needs are booked, or the shipper taps Enough Trucks, the other offers close.

cancel.title: Changing your mind
cancel.body: A shipper or an owner can cancel a booking while it is pending or confirmed, before the goods are loaded. Once a truck is on the road, the trip has to be finished. Drivers cannot cancel a booking; they call the owner.

hero.title: Know who is moving your goods
hero.lead: Every booking on FLITO is between people whose identity has been checked, in trucks whose papers have been checked, with a record of every step.

pillars.title: Checked identities
pillars.body: Owners and drivers upload a citizenship card, national ID, passport or driving license. The FLITO team checks the name and photo before they can make offers or take jobs. Verified people carry a badge.

pillars.title: Checked trucks
pillars.body: Owners add each truck's registration number, bluebook, and insurance if they have it. A verified truck carries the same badge.

pillars.title: Numbers only where needed
pillars.body: Phone numbers are shown only to the shipper, owner and driver on a booking, and hidden again if it is cancelled.

pillars.title: Location only during the trip
pillars.body: Only the assigned driver can share a location, and only while the booking is in transit. The shipper and owner see it; nobody else.

pillars.title: Proof at both ends
pillars.body: Photos at pickup and drop-off, and the receiver's signature on the driver's phone, are kept on the booking.

pillars.title: Ratings after every trip
pillars.body: Shippers and owners rate each other once a job is done, so good work is seen.

account.title: Keeping your account safe
points: Passwords and PINs are stored only as one-way hashes, never as plain text
Five wrong PINs lock PIN login for a while, and each lock lasts longer than the last
Email codes expire after 15 minutes, work once and stop after 5 wrong tries
Never share your PIN, password or an email code, not even with someone who says they are from FLITO
FLITO will never ask you to pay into a personal account to unlock a load

tips.title: Safety tips for each role
shipper: Book owners with the verified badge and good ratings
Describe the goods honestly, with the real weight
Pack fragile goods well and photograph them before loading
Make sure someone is at the drop-off to sign
owner: Send only trucks that are roadworthy, insured and have valid papers
Assign drivers who hold a valid license for that truck
Check the goods match the load description before loading
Keep your drivers' phone numbers up to date
driver: Never drive tired, and rest on long hill routes
Keep within the truck's legal load limit
Tap each step only when it really happens
Do not carry goods that are not on the booking

prohibited.title: Goods that cannot be moved through FLITO
prohibited.lead: These are banned on every booking. Anything else that needs a permit must travel with that permit.
items: Wildlife, animal parts and protected plants or timber without permits
Stolen goods, or goods hidden from customs
Hazardous chemicals or fuel without the required permits and a suitable truck
People. FLITO is only for goods

report.title: Something wrong?
report.body: If a person, truck or booking does not seem right, contact the FLITO team with the booking details. We can suspend accounts that break the rules.

emergency.title: In an emergency on the road
emergency.lead: Call the emergency services first, then let the other people on the booking know.

hero.title: We're making trucking in Nepal work better for everyone on the road
hero.lead: FLITO is a truck booking platform for Nepal. We connect the people who need goods moved with the truck owners and drivers who move them, and we make sure each side can trust the other.

what.title: What FLITO is
body: FLITO is a marketplace. Shippers post the goods they need moved. Truck owners whose trucks fit send offers. When a price is agreed, a booking is made, the owner assigns a driver, and everyone follows the trip to delivery.
We don't own trucks and we don't employ drivers. We build the tools and run the checks that let owners, drivers and shippers find each other and work together with confidence.

name.title: The name
name.body: FLITO stands for Freight & Load Interchange for Truck Operations: a place where freight and loads change hands between the people who have them and the trucks that can carry them.

who.title: Three kinds of people, one trip

roles.shipper: Traders, shops, factories, farmers' groups and families who need goods moved, once or every week.
roles.owner: People and companies with one truck or a fleet, who want fewer empty trips and steady work.
roles.driver: The people behind the wheel, added by their owner, with a simple job screen and a phone-and-PIN login.

items.title: Fair prices
items.body: Prices are agreed openly between shipper and owner, offer by offer, never set behind closed doors.

items.title: Trust you can see
items.body: A verified badge means our team has checked the ID or the truck's papers. We would rather go slower than verify carelessly.

items.title: Made for Nepal
items.body: Nepali first, BS dates, ward-level addresses and phone-and-PIN login, because that is how people here work.

items.title: Simple for everyone
items.body: Big text, big buttons and one job per screen, so a first-time smartphone user can use FLITO as easily as anyone.

hero.title: No truck in Nepal should drive home empty.
hero.lead: Our mission is to fill Nepal's trucks both ways: more income for the people who own and drive them, fairer prices for the people who need goods moved, and fewer empty kilometres on our roads.

story.title: It started with a truck yard
paragraphs: Spend an evening at any truck yard in Nepal and you will hear the same story. A truck came up full from the border or an industrial town. It unloaded in the city. Now the driver is waiting, calling contacts, asking around for anything going back. Sometimes a load turns up after a day or two. Often the truck simply goes home empty.

The same trip looks different from the other side. A shop in a hill town needs goods brought up. A trader has a load to send down to the Terai. They phone the people they know, take whatever price is offered and hope the truck turns up on time. Neither side can see the other, even when they are standing in the same town on the same day.
FLITO exists to put those two sides on one screen. When an owner can see the loads going their way, and a shipper can see the trucks already heading there, the empty trip becomes a paid one.

mission.quote: An empty truck isn't a lack of goods to move. It's a lack of information about where those goods are.

problems.title: Who pays for an empty trip

items.title: Truck owners
items.body: A return trip with nothing on it still costs diesel, tolls, wear and a driver's wages. That cost comes out of the loaded trip's profit.

items.title: Shippers
items.body: Prices have to cover the empty return, and without a way to compare, there is little room to ask for better.

items.title: Drivers
items.body: Days waiting in yards, away from family, for a load that may never come.

change.title: What a full return trip means

items.title: More from every truck
items.body: A paid return trip can turn a thin margin into a real income for an owner with one or two trucks.

items.title: Fairer prices
items.body: When trucks are not priced for an empty return, and offers can be compared, shippers pay a fairer rate.

items.title: Fewer empty kilometres
items.body: Moving the same goods in fewer trips means less diesel burnt and less traffic on hill roads.

items.title: Trust between strangers
items.body: Checked IDs, checked trucks and a record of every trip let people work with someone they have never met.

commitments.title: What we commit to
items: Be open about how FLITO works and what it costs, before anyone pays anything
Check every owner, driver and truck before they can take a job
Collect only the data a trip needs, and never sell it
Build for the least confident user first: Nepali first, big text, phone-and-PIN login
Listen to the drivers and owners who use FLITO every day, and change what doesn't work for them

hero.title: How can we help?
hero.lead: Answers to the questions people ask most, from signing up to getting paid.

stillNeed.title: Still need help?
stillNeed.body: The FLITO team reads every message. Tell us your phone number or email and, if it's about a trip, the booking.

items.q: Do I need an email address to use FLITO?
items.a: No. You can sign up with just your phone number and a 4-digit PIN. You can also sign up with an email and password, or with your Google account.

items.q: I forgot my PIN. What do I do?
a: If you are a driver, ask your truck owner: they can set a new PIN for you from their fleet page.
If you signed up yourself with a phone number, contact the FLITO team from the Contact page with the number on your account.

items.q: I forgot my password.
items.a: On the Log in page, tap "Forgot password?" and enter your email. We send a 6-digit code that works for 15 minutes. Enter it with your new password.

items.q: Can I change from Nepali to English?
items.a: Yes, at any time. Tap the EN / ने switch at the top of the screen, or go to Settings → Language & region. You can also choose BS or AD dates there.

items.q: How do I switch to dark mode?
items.a: Tap the sun or moon at the top of the screen, or go to Settings → Appearance and choose Light, Dark or Match device.

items.q: How do I post a load?
items.a: Tap "Post a Load" and follow the steps: what you are sending, how much it weighs, pickup and drop-off addresses, and the pickup day. Photos are optional but help owners give a good price.

items.q: Can my load go on more than one truck?
items.a: Yes. When you post it, choose how many trucks it needs, up to 10. The weight is shared equally, every accepted truck is its own booking with its own driver and delivery proof, and you can tap Enough Trucks once you have what you need.

items.q: How long does my load stay open?
items.a: A load takes offers until the end of its pickup day, Nepal time, and for at least 12 hours after you post it. If no truck is booked by then, it expires and you can post it again.

items.q: Can I choose a truck myself?
items.a: Yes. Open your load and tap "Choose a Truck". FLITO lists trucks that can carry it and are free on that day, nearest first, and you can ask an owner to carry it at your price.

items.q: Do I have to be verified to post a load?
items.a: No. Shippers can post loads and book trucks without verification. Verifying your identity still helps owners trust your loads.

items.q: How are prices decided?
items.a: There are no fixed rates. An owner offers a price for each truck, or a shipper asks a matched truck at their own price. The other side accepts or declines it at that price, with no back-and-forth.

items.q: How long does an offer last?
items.a: 48 hours, and never longer than its load.

items.q: Why can't I send an offer?
items.a: Truck owners need a verified identity before sending offers. Go to Profile → Identity verification, upload your documents and wait for the FLITO team to approve them.

items.q: Does FLITO charge a fee?
items.a: Shippers pay nothing, and joining, posting loads and sending offers stay free. Truck owners pay FLITO a small fee on each completed trip. The exact fee is shown before you send an offer, on the booking and on your monthly bill, so you always know it before you take a trip. Fees start on 1 Magh 2083 (15 January 2027); trips booked before then are free, and so are each owner's first 5 trips after that. Cancelled trips have no fee. Trips are billed each Nepali month and paid by the 15th of the next.

items.q: How do owners pay FLITO's fees?
items.a: Open Profile, then FLITO fees. It shows each month's bill and FLITO's official bank, eSewa and Khalti accounts with their QR codes. Pay with your own bank app or wallet, then tap "I have paid FLITO". The fee counts as paid once FLITO finds the money in its account. If fees stay unpaid after the due date, your new offers are paused until you pay; trips already booked carry on.

items.q: When can I see the other person's phone number?
items.a: Once a booking is made, the shipper, owner and driver on it can call each other in one tap. Numbers are never shown on loads or offers, and are hidden again if the booking is cancelled.

items.q: How does tracking work?
items.a: While the booking is in transit, the driver can share their location from the job screen. The shipper and owner see the truck on the map. Sharing stops when the trip ends.

items.q: Can I cancel a booking?
items.a: A shipper or owner can cancel while the booking is pending or confirmed, before loading. Once the goods are in transit, the trip must be finished. Drivers can't cancel; they call their owner.

items.q: How is a delivery confirmed?
items.a: At the drop-off, the driver photographs the goods and the receiver signs on the driver's phone. Both are kept on the booking.

items.q: How do ratings work?
items.a: After a booking is completed, the shipper rates the owner and the owner rates the shipper, once each, from 1 to 5 stars.

items.q: Which documents do I need?
a: Everyone verifies with one ID: a citizenship card (both sides), national ID (both sides), passport photo page or driving license.
Truck owners also add their PAN document. Drivers add their driving license. A company registration is optional for owners.

items.q: How long does verification take?
items.a: The FLITO team reviews documents in the order they arrive and checks each one by hand. You get a notification as soon as yours are approved, or told what to fix.

items.q: My documents were rejected. What now?
items.a: Open Identity verification to see the reason, replace the document that needs fixing and submit again.

items.q: Why can't I change my name?
items.a: Your name is matched to your identity documents, so it is locked while they are under review or approved.

items.q: How do I pay for a trip?
items.a: The shipper pays the truck owner directly. On the booking, the shipper sees the owner's bank account, eSewa or Khalti with its QR code. Pay with your own bank app or wallet (or in cash, as you agree), then tap "I have paid" and add the transaction ID. The owner confirms the money arrived.

items.q: Does the money go through FLITO?
items.a: No. A trip's money goes straight from the shipper to the owner's own account; FLITO only keeps the record. FLITO will never ask you to send money to unlock a load or an account, and never asks for your PIN, password or OTP.

items.q: How do owners add their bank account or QR?
items.a: Open Profile, then Payment details, and add a bank account, eSewa or Khalti with a photo of its payment QR. Only shippers with a booking with you see them.

items.q: Where do drivers see their earnings?
items.a: Drivers have an Earnings page that lists the trips they completed.
